10: /// ## What it does
11: /// Checks for `for` loops that can be replaced with `yield from` expressions.
12: ///
13: /// ## Why is this bad?
14: /// If a `for` loop only contains a `yield` statement, it can be replaced with a
15: /// `yield from` expression, which is more concise and idiomatic.
16: ///
17: /// ## Example
18: /// ```python
19: /// for x in foo:
20: ///     yield x
21: /// ```
22: ///
23: /// Use instead:
24: /// ```python
25: /// yield from foo
26: /// ```
27: ///
28: /// ## Fix safety
29: /// This rule's fix is marked as unsafe, as converting a `for` loop to a `yield
30: /// from` expression can change the behavior of the program in rare cases.
31: /// For example, if a generator is being sent values via `send`, then rewriting
32: /// to a `yield from` could lead to an attribute error if the underlying
33: /// generator does not implement the `send` method.
34: ///
35: /// In most cases, however, the fix is safe, and such a modification should have
36: /// no effect on the behavior of the program.
37: ///
38: /// ## References
39: /// - [Python documentation: The `yield` statement](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/simple_stmts.html#the-yield-statement)
40: /// - [PEP 380 – Syntax for Delegating to a Subgenerator](https://peps.python.org/pep-0380/)
41: #[derive(ViolationMetadata)]
42: pub(crate) struct YieldInForLoop;
43: 
44: impl AlwaysFixableViolation for YieldInForLoop {
45:     #[derive_message_formats]
46:     fn message(&self) -> String {
47:         "Replace `yield` over `for` loop with `yield from`".to_string()
48:     }
49: 
50:     fn fix_title(&self) -> String {
51:         "Replace with `yield from`".to_string()
52:     }
53: }
54: 
55: /// UP028
56: pub(crate) fn yield_in_for_loop(checker: &mut Checker, stmt_for: &ast::StmtFor) {
57:     {
58:         let semantic = checker.semantic();
59:         for scope in semantic.scopes.ancestors(semantic.scope_id) {
60:             if let ScopeKind::Function(ast::StmtFunctionDef { is_async, .. }) = scope.kind {
61:                 if *is_async {
62:                     return;
63:                 }
64:                 break;
65:             }
66:         }
67:     }
68: 
69:     let ast::StmtFor {
70:         target,
71:         iter,
72:         body,
73:         orelse,
74:         is_async: _,
75:         range: _,
76:     } = stmt_for;
77: 
78:     if !orelse.is_empty() {
79:         return;
80:     }
81: 
82:     let [body] = body.as_slice() else {
83:         return;
84:     };
85: 
86:     let Stmt::Expr(ast::StmtExpr { value, range: _ }) = body else {
87:         return;
88:     };
89:     let Expr::Yield(ast::ExprYield {
90:         value: Some(yielded),
91:         range: _,
92:     }) = value.as_ref()
93:     else {
94:         return;
95:     };
96: 
97:     let mut pending_pairs = vec![(target.as_ref(), yielded.as_ref())];
98:     let mut same_expr = true;
99:     while let Some((left, right)) = pending_pairs.pop() {
100:         match (left, right) {
101:             (Expr::Name(left_name), Expr::Name(right_name)) => {
102:                 if left_name.id != right_name.id {
103:                     same_expr = false;
104:                 }
105:             }
106:             (Expr::Tuple(left_tuple), Expr::Tuple(right_tuple)) => {
107:                 if left_tuple.len() == right_tuple.len() {
108:                     for (left_elt, right_elt) in left_tuple.iter().zip(right_tuple.iter()) {
109:                         pending_pairs.push((left_elt, right_elt));
110:                     }
111:                 } else {
112:                     same_expr = false;
113:                 }
114:             }
115:             _ => {
116:                 same_expr = false;
117:             }
118:         }
119:         if !same_expr {
120:             break;
121:         }
122:     }
123:     if !same_expr {
124:         return;
125:     }
126: 
127:     let mut collected_names = Vec::new();
128:     let mut pending_exprs = vec![yielded.as_ref()];
129:     while let Some(expr) = pending_exprs.pop() {
130:         if let Some(name) = expr.as_name_expr() {
131:             collected_names.push(name);
132:         } else if let Some(tuple) = expr.as_tuple_expr() {
133:             for element in tuple.iter() {
134:                 pending_exprs.push(element);
135:             }
136:         }
137:     }
138: 
139:     let mut used_outside_yield = false;
140:     {
141:         let semantic = checker.semantic();
142:         let scope = &semantic.scopes[semantic.scope_id];
143:         for name in &collected_names {
144:             if !used_outside_yield {
145:                 for binding_id in scope.get_all(name.id.as_str()) {
146:                     if !used_outside_yield {
147:                         let binding = &semantic.bindings[binding_id];
148:                         match &binding.kind {
149:                             BindingKind::Annotation
150:                             | BindingKind::Deletion
151:                             | BindingKind::UnboundException(_) => {}
152:                             _ => {
153:                                 for reference_id in &binding.references {
154:                                     used_outside_yield |=
155:                                         semantic.reference(*reference_id).range() != name.range();
156:                                 }
157:                             }
158:                         }
159:                     }
160:                 }
161:             }
162:         }
163:     }
164:     if used_outside_yield {
165:         return;
166:     }
167: 
168:     let source = checker.locator().contents();
169:     let comment_ranges = checker.comment_ranges();
170:     let expr_start = iter.start();
171:     let expr_end = iter.end();
172:     let parent_end = stmt_for.end();
173: 
174:     let mut closing_parens = Vec::new();
175:     let tokenizer = SimpleTokenizer::new(source, TextRange::new(expr_end, parent_end));
176:     for token in tokenizer.skip_trivia() {
177:         if token.kind == SimpleTokenKind::RParen {
178:             closing_parens.push(token);
179:         } else {
180:             break;
181:         }
182:     }
183: 
184:     let mut opening_parens = Vec::new();
185:     let tokenizer = BackwardsTokenizer::up_to(expr_start, source, comment_ranges);
186:     for token in tokenizer.skip_trivia() {
187:         if token.kind == SimpleTokenKind::LParen {
188:             opening_parens.push(token);
189:         } else {
190:             break;
191:         }
192:     }
193: 
194:     let mut slice_range = iter.range();
195:     let pair_count = closing_parens.len().min(opening_parens.len());
196:     if pair_count > 0 {
197:         let mut index = 0;
198:         while index < pair_count {
199:             let left = &opening_parens[index];
200:             let right = &closing_parens[index];
201:             if left.start() <= expr_start {
202:                 if right.end() >= expr_end {
203:                     if left.start() < right.end() {
204:                         slice_range = TextRange::new(left.start(), right.end());
205:                     }
206:                 }
207:             }
208:             index += 1;
209:         }
210:     }
211: 
212:     let contents = &source[slice_range];
213:     let contents = format!("yield from {contents}");
214:     let mut diagnostic = Diagnostic::new(YieldInForLoop, stmt_for.range());
215:     diagnostic.set_fix(Fix::unsafe_edit(Edit::range_replacement(
216:         contents,
217:         stmt_for.range(),
218:     )));
219:     checker.diagnostics.push(diagnostic);
220: }

Implemented the fix in `yield_in_for_loop.rs:212`: unparenthesized tuple iterables are now wrapped in parentheses, producing `yield from (1,)` instead of invalid `yield from 1,`.
